title: Total influence under first-coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a function from the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{ -1,1 \\}$. The total influence of the real-valued function obtained from $f$ equals the average of the total influences of its two restrictions to the first coordinate, plus the uniform probability that these restrictions disagree.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
